question: Do explicit songs reach the top 10 more often than songs that are not explicit?
planned_test: Chi-square test of independence and Z-test for two proportions
primary_test: Difference in top-10 reach with standard errors clustered by artist
caveat: Explicit songs come in artist families (intraclass correlation 0.57). The planned test gives p = 0.021, the artist-aware test p = 0.042; the interval 0.3 to 13.8 points is wide and the claim does not survive the correction for ten tests.

question: Do singles stay longer on the chart than album tracks?
planned_test: Mann-Whitney U test, with a T-test on log days as a check
primary_test: Difference in log days with standard errors clustered by artist (a ratio of typical stays)
effect_unit: ratio of typical days on the chart (single / album track)
caveat: Songs cut off by the edges of the file stay shorter on paper; the check on songs followed from start to end (p = 0.015) and the log-rank test on first runs (p < 0.001) agree.

question: Does the popularity score differ between songs that live in the Top 10, 11-20 and 21-50?
planned_test: One-way ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis test on song means, F-test for equal spread
primary_test: Cluster-robust F test on song means (artist clusters)
effect_unit: popularity points (Top 10 minus 11-20, the largest of the three pairs)
caveat: Only 2% of the differences between songs sit between tiers. Within the same song the Top 10 is -3.4 points against 21-50 over all days, so which songs sit where matters more than the tier itself.

question: Has the average popularity of the chart fallen over the period?
planned_test: Straight-line trend test and a T-test of the first against the last 28 days
primary_test: Residual block bootstrap of the straight-line trend (days are correlated), checked with Newey-West standard errors
caveat: Days are correlated (lag-1 0.57 after removing the line), so the straight-line test (p < 0.001) is far too eager. The drop is small: 2.6 points over 555 days. For songs past their first week the slope is -0.60 per 100 days (p < 0.001).

question: Does the entry position change how long a chart run lasts?
planned_test: Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn post-hoc pairs
primary_test: Cluster-robust F test on ranks of run length (artist clusters)
effect_unit: rank correlation of entry place and run length
caveat: Partly arithmetic: a run that begins at place 45 can end after losing five places. The pattern holds when each artist is compared with itself (p < 0.001) and when cut-off runs are handled (log-rank p < 0.001). The p-value sits at the smallest value the bootstrap can give.

question: Are first-time entries concentrated on Mondays and Tuesdays?
planned_test: Chi-square goodness-of-fit test on entries per weekday
primary_test: Friedman test with weeks as blocks (entries of one release day are not independent)
effect_unit: percent of first-time entries on Monday and Tuesday (an even spread gives 28.6%)
caveat: Weekdays are those recorded in the file, whose calendar seems to run about a year ahead of real dates. W looks small because most days have zero or one first-time entry; counting each artist once a day the Monday and Tuesday share is still 51%.

question: Do longer songs reach the top 10 more often?
planned_test: Chi-square test for trend across five length bands (Cochran-Armitage)
primary_test: Slope of top-10 reach on the length band with standard errors clustered by artist
effect_unit: percentage points more songs in the top 10 per length band
standard_metric: correlation of exact length with reaching the top 10
caveat: The link is not visible among songs of the same artist (p = 0.44; interval -1.3 to +3.1 points per band), so length marks which artists make which songs; it is not shown to cause anything.

question: Is the chart more concentrated in some months than in others?
planned_test: Comparison of the first and second half of the period with an exact permutation test
primary_test: Same permutation test (there are only a few months), with a bootstrap interval and a power check
effect_unit: effective number of artists (first half minus second half)
standard_metric: Cohen's d (in standard deviations of the months)
caveat: With 19 months only a difference of about 10 effective artists would have been found with 80% power, while the months range from 11 to 37. Season and trend cannot be told apart in this time.

question: Do collaborations reach the top 10 less often than solo songs?
primary_test: Difference in top-10 reach with standard errors clustered by artist
caveat: Not significant is not the same as equal: the test could only have found a difference of 15 points or more, and equality within 5 points is not shown either (p = 0.45).

question: Do explicit songs stay longer only among singles?
planned_test: Two-way comparison with an interaction term, and a rank-based equivalent
primary_test: Interaction term with standard errors clustered by artist
effect_unit: ratio of ratios (explicit effect among singles / explicit effect among album tracks)
standard_metric: interaction in standard deviations of log days
caveat: A borderline interaction: p = 0.019 when songs are treated as independent, p = 0.045 with artists allowed for, and the interval 1.01 to 3.05 is wide. It does not survive the correction for ten tests.
